chunks: "Balance charging means charging a series pack so that every cell ends up at the same voltage, not just the pack total at the right voltage.
In a series string all cells get the same charge current, but they don't start at the same state of charge and they don't have exactly the same capacity. So one cell reaches 4.
2 volts before the others. If the charger only watches the pack voltage, it keeps going and pushes that cell past 4. 2 volts while the others are still lower.
That damages the cell and is a safety risk. With balance charging there's an extra connector with a tap to every cell node, so the charger or BMS can see each cell.
2 volts, it bleeds that cell through a small resistor, or in active schemes moves the energy to weaker cells, while the others keep charging until all are about 4. 2 volts.
You need it for any series pack, 2S and up, and especially for old or mismatched cells and for any pack you fast charge.
A single cell, or cells that are only in parallel, don't need it because parallel cells equalize themselves."
